title: The Gap Between AI and the Real World
summary: We built Reducto for the world’s hardest documents - now we’re building for the world’s data in its entirety.
body_markdown:
We started Reducto around a simple, maybe obvious, idea. Models have been impressively intelligent since 2023 but we believe that intelligence matters most when it’s applied to real world data and context.
Three years later the world has seen model capabilities push frontiers in math, science, and software engineering, but the way the broader world operates seems almost untouched. There’s an absurd gap between SF’s frenetic enthusiasm for AI, and the mundanity of how key systems across industries like healthcare, finance, and insurance are actually run to this day.


The first question that I struggle to answer is – *why* ?


I’m drawn to answers that are exciting but the most honest answer is much simpler. The use of fax in healthcare persists decades after inventing better technology for communication. Humans have ways of working that are filled with idiosyncrasies and inefficiencies; we build around systems that are familiar and adapt around problems like information silos in our organizations.


Making real progress for the world means being excited about solving the boring problems that gate it. Reducto chose a very specific one to dedicate itself to:


**Documents**


A lot of the world’s most important data is in file formats that weren’t built for language models. PDF as a format was created for printers to faithfully print documents and somehow became a status quo across decades.


We weren’t the first company to think about PDF processing but we started the company at a very special moment in time. Hundreds of “Intelligent Document Processing” companies before us used tools like OCR to solve for very specific pipelines. Even today, institutions like banks run on pipelines that were carefully built to handle a constrained set of document inputs with layers of human review to fix errors. These pipelines were too brittle to extend and capped the ambition of teams that wanted to automate more.


We believed that was too serious of a bottleneck to accept.


We believe documents are artifacts of human work and knowledge. Contracts reflect agreements between entities, medical records document years of clinical judgement, and research papers share discoveries for others to build on.


The information within them is incredibly important for the world but the files are imperfect and unlocking that information is actually really hard.


The first problem for us to solve as a company was to be able to read that data as accurately as a human could. We don’t think our customers should restrict their ambition to the normal cases, so we set out to address the accuracy problems that exist in the long tail. Our customers shouldn’t have to think about whether an invoice was rotated, whether a bank statement contained a challenging table, or if a healthcare record had messy handwriting.


We’ve worked relentlessly to break the accuracy standard in the industry over the last few years. Candidly, we’re excited to see others attempt to compete for that frontier and we haven’t wavered in our commitment to giving our customers the best outputs possible.


But I don’t think we’ve realized our potential as a company.


**Our mandate**


The best version of Reducto is one where it’s the natural interface between human data and models. Our job is to be a frictionless set of tools for models to use on every interaction they have with a document.


We’ve trained incredibly capable models, but we were originally so focused on addressing the accuracy problems that we did so at the cost of latency and price. Reducto has been a natural choice for the world’s *hardest* data, but we want to be a natural choice for the world’s data in its entirety.


We want to do that without compromising on what makes Reducto great.


There are many libraries that prioritize cost and latency at the expense of accuracy but if we’re building a world where models will act on this data in ways that have real consequences for real people, that risk of mistakes should not be acceptable.


**Reducto will deliver premium accuracy without the premium.**


We’re going to make our capabilities accessible to everyone, across use cases and across interaction modalities. We will solve for the full life cycle of document work and bridge the gaps not only in parsing and reading data, but also in editing and generation. We will continue delivering incredible models and complement them with the tooling and infrastructure needed for production pipelines.


Later this week we’ll be launching a new product as a step towards this broader mandate.


As a team we are more than excited to run after the unglamorous problems for our customers so they can build without bottlenecks.


More from us soon.


- Adit Abraham
*CEO, Reducto*
